title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, meaning the boundary of the moduli space of ν-pointed curves. On the previous page Grothendieck takes a 'standard' (nodal, marked) curve X over an algebraically closed field k. He calls such a configuration a 'singularity', i.e. a point at infinity of M_{g,ν}. Notation:
- X̂ is the complete curve.
- X̃ (more precisely the normalization of X̂) has components X_α, α ∈ S, of genus g_α.
- A is the set of double points (nodes). Ã → S assigns to each branch the component it lies on.
- I is the set of marked points (points at infinity).
- The dual graph G_X has vertex set S and edge set A.

He has shown π_0(G_X) ≅ π_0(X). For connected X he defines g(X̂) = dim H^1(X̂, O) and χ_coh = 1 − g. Formula (13) reads χ_coh(X̂) = Σ_α (1 − g_α) − card A.

This page:
- (15) defines h_1 = rk_Z H_1(G_X, Z), the first Betti number (cyclomatic number) of the dual graph.
- Proof of (13), called 'standard': use the normalization sequence 0 → O_X̂ → ν_* O_{X̃} → ⊕_{a∈A} k(a) → 0 and take Euler characteristics.
- Euler–Poincaré for the connected graph gives χ(G_X) = h_0 − h_1 = 1 − h_1 = card S − card A. Hence h_1 = 1 − card S + card A.
- Substituting gives (14): g(X̂) = Σ_α g_α + h_1. This is the classical arithmetic-genus formula for a nodal curve.

Corollary. g(X̂) depends only on the combinatorial data of the 'singularity': the dual graph with its vertex genera. It is therefore called the genus of the singularity (marginal note: 'déf = genre de G'). The type of a singularity is the pair (g, ν), where ν = card I is the 'marked weight'. The page then begins defining the marked weight of a vertex, ν_α = card I_α. On the next page this leads to the total weight ν̂_α = ν_α + valence, and to the stability condition 2g_α − 2 + ν̂_α ≥ 1, which he phrases as 'anabelian' components.

Purpose: to attach to each boundary point of M̄_{g,ν} a combinatorial invariant (a weighted, marked dual graph, which he will call an 'MD-graph'). This sets up the stratification at infinity by graph types.
errors: On the previous page, (14) is written as card S + card A + 1; the correct expression is −card S + card A + 1 = h_1. This page's derivation 1 − card S + card A = h_1 gets the sign right and silently corrects it.

The corollary is phrased loosely: g(X̂) depends on the vertex genera g_α and the graph G_X, not on the 'singularities' in the sense of nodes alone. Given Grothendieck's usage ('singularity' = the whole marked stable configuration), this is a wording issue, not a mathematical one.
The 'Démonstration standard (!)' only sketches the normalization exact sequence. This is fine, since it is classical.

ideas.what: Arithmetic genus of a connected nodal curve equals the sum of component genera plus the first Betti number of the dual graph
ideas.modern_name: genus formula for nodal curves / dual graph genus g = Σ g_v + b_1(Γ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Severi/Hartshorne-type exercise); standard in Deligne–Mumford 1969 and stable-curve literature
ideas.where_published: Standard in Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen; possibly implicit in SGA 7 discussions of semistable reduction

ideas.what: Proof via normalization exact sequence and Euler–Poincaré characteristic of the graph
Attaching to a boundary point of M_{g,ν} a combinatorial type: dual graph with vertex genera and marked-point weights; 'type' (g, ν)
ideas.modern_name: stable (modular) graph / weighted dual graph indexing boundary strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983; graph formalism systematized by Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the 'tour de Teichmüller' and the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} but not this explicit formalism

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only the classical genus formula for nodal curves and the start of a definition of weighted dual graph types. This material is fully standard. Its only interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck setting up the stable-graph combinatorics for the boundary of M_{g,ν}, in the spirit of the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: 'g(\hat x) = Σ_{α∈S} g(α) + h_1' should read 'g(X̂) = Σ_{α∈S} g_α + h_1'.
In the corollary, 'des les singularités de X' is more likely 'de la singularité X' or 'de la singularité de X'. Grothendieck uses 'singularité' for the whole marked nodal configuration.
'(\bar g, ν)' is probably simply '(g, ν)'.
The struck-through word after 'où' at the top is illegible ('[-...-]' is fine). In 'χ(G_X) = h_0 − h_1', a struck fragment follows h_0, and the underbrace under h_0 is '1'.
